paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love about this chapter. It's a LIST, and God had Moses write it down. The Bible says, "At the LORD’s command, Moses recorded the stages of their journey" (Numbers 33:2). Every camp, every stop, every dusty "set out and camp" mattered enough to keep.

So what does that teach us? The long stretches count too. The wilderness had a spring-and-palm-tree stop (Numbers 33:9), a no-water stop (Numbers 33:14), and a hard goodbye when Aaron died on Mount Hor (Numbers 33:38). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and I'd have told you nothing was happening back there. This chapter says the road is worth remembering, even the parts that felt like waiting.

Now look where the list ends: on the plains of Moab, by the Jordan, across from Jericho (Numbers 33:48). They started by marching out of Egypt in full view of everyone (Numbers 33:3), and they kept moving, stop after stop, until they reached the river. So here's your big idea, baker: keep taking the next step, because the One who sends you out is the One who keeps the record. Some days you'll feel like you're just packing up and camping again, and that is still the journey. Keep going!
